title_en: Cixi Bosheng Plastic Products Co., Ltd. v. Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: 1. In a dispute over intellectual property infringement involving an e-commerce platform, where an operator within the platform applies to the People's Court for behavioral preservation, requesting an order to the e-commerce platform operator to restore links and services, the People's Court shall examine the application and render a ruling after comprehensively considering factors such as whether the operator's request has a factual basis and legal grounds, whether failure to restore would cause irreparable harm to the operator within the platform, whether the harm that restoration might cause to the IP right holder would outweigh the harm caused by maintaining the measures against the operator within the platform, whether restoration would harm social public interest, and whether there are other circumstances making restoration inappropriate. If the People's Court orders restoration, the e-commerce platform operator shall cancel the previously adopted measures.

full_text_en:
Cixi Bosheng Plastic Products Co., Ltd. v. Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent

【Ruling Summary】

I. In a dispute over intellectual property infringement involving an e-commerce platform, where a platform operator files an application with the people's court for a preservation order to request that the e-commerce platform operator restore links, services, and the like, the people's court shall review the application and make a ruling by comprehensively considering factors such as whether the platform operator's request has a factual basis and legal foundation; whether failure to restore would cause irreparable harm to the platform operator; whether the harm that restoration may cause to the intellectual property right holder would exceed the harm that maintaining the relevant measures would cause to the platform operator; whether restoration would harm the public interest; and whether there are other circumstances that render restoration inappropriate. Where the people's court orders restoration, the e-commerce platform operator shall immediately revoke the measures previously taken.

II. Where a platform operator applies for a preservation order as mentioned in the preceding paragraph, it shall provide security in accordance with the law. The people's court may order the platform operator not to withdraw a certain amount of funds from the payment collection account used for the sale of the allegedly infringing product on the e-commerce platform until a final judgment is rendered, as security. Such amount may be the infringing gains of the platform operator, i.e., the product of the unit price of the allegedly infringing product, the profit margin, the contribution rate of the patent in question to the product's profit, and the sales volume of the allegedly infringing product after the e-commerce platform operator revokes the relevant measures.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 993

Applicant (Appellant, Defendant at First Instance): Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: Meilong Village, Longshan Town, Yongkang City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Huiliang, Executive Director and Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Ding Lei, attorney at Beijing Centaline (Shanghai) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 506, 5th Floor, Building 3, No. 969, Wen Yi Xi Road, Wuchang Street, Yuhang District, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Fan, Chairman and General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Kong Shanshan, attorney at Beijing Jiarun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ma Hui, attorney at Beijing Jiarun Law Firm.

Respondent (Appellee, Plaintiff at First Instance): Cixi Bosheng Plastic Products Co., Ltd. Domicile: Dongdu Village, Longshan Town, Cixi City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Huang Chunya, Executive Director and General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Yan Xiao, patent agent at Cixi Fangsheng Patent Agency (General Partnership).

In the case of the dispute over infringement of utility model patent brought by appellant Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lianyue Company) and Zhejiang Xinghao Plastic Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinghao Company) against appellee Cixi Bosheng Plastic Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bosheng Company), and respondents at first instance Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tmall Company) and Xie Hui, the applicant Lianyue Company filed an application for a preservation order with this Court on November 5, 2020, requesting that this Court order Tmall Company to immediately restore the sales link for the "hand-free mop, household flat lazy absorbent mop cloth, net red mop that cleans with one drag, dry and wet dual-use, Douyin floor cleaning tool" (hereinafter referred to as the allegedly infringing product) on the "Bangzhufu Flagship Store" (hereinafter referred to as the involved online shop) operated on "Tmall.com," until the date when the final judgment takes effect. The applicant Lianyue Company agreed to provide security in the amount of RMB 6.32 million held in its Alipay account balance.

After a hearing, this Court preliminarily finds the following facts:

Bosheng Company is the patentee of the following two patents: 1. Utility model patent No. ZL201820084323.7, titled "Flat Mop Cleaning Tool with Novel Bucket Structure" (hereinafter referred to as the patent in question). 2. Utility model patent No. ZL201620853180.2, titled "Mop Bucket for Wringing and Cleaning a Flat Mop" (hereinafter referred to as the 180.2 patent). On October 11, 2019, Bosheng Company filed the present case and another case separately with the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province, on the ground that the allegedly infringing product infringed the above two patents. The case number of the present case at first instance is (2019) Zhe 02 Zhi Min Chu No. 367; the case number of the other case is (2019) Zhe 02 Zhi Min Chu No. 368 (hereinafter referred to as Case No. 368). In both cases, Bosheng Company requested the court to order Lianyue Company, Xinghao Company, and Xie Hui to immediately cease the acts of manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale the allegedly infringing product; to order Tmall Company to immediately delete and disconnect the sales link for the allegedly infringing product; and to order Xinghao Company, Lianyue Company, and Tmall Company to jointly and severally compensate Bosheng Company for economic losses of RMB 3.16 million. On October 15, 2019, Bosheng Company applied to the court of first instance for property preservation in both cases. On October 29, 2019, the court of first instance issued a property preservation ruling, freezing the Alipay account balance or bank deposits of Lianyue Company in the amount of RMB 3.16 million in each of the two cases. As of now, the above two sums remain frozen. On October 20, 2019, and November 25, 2019, Bosheng Company filed complaints with Tmall Company regarding the above two cases. Lianyue Company filed an objection and, on November 10, 2019, issued a "Letter of Commitment for Intellectual Property Guarantee," agreeing to deposit a guarantee of RMB 1 million into its Alipay account and consenting to Alipay Company and Tmall Company freezing all sales revenue from its online shop from 10:00 p.m. on November 10, 2019.

On April 10, 2020, the court of first instance rendered a judgment in the present case, ordering: Xie Hui, Xinghao Company, and Lianyue Company to immediately cease the infringing acts; Tmall Company to immediately delete and disconnect the sales link for the allegedly infringing product; and Xinghao Company and Lianyue Company to jointly and severally compensate Bosheng Company for economic losses of RMB 3.16 million. On the same day, Bosheng Company again filed a complaint with Tmall Company regarding the allegedly infringing product. On April 17, 2020, Tmall Company deleted the sales link for the allegedly infringing product. Lianyue Company and Xinghao Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court. During the second-instance trial of this case, the China National Intellectual Property Administration, on September 9, 2020, issued a review decision on the invalidation declaration request for the patent in question, finding that claims 1-24 of the patent in question all lacked novelty as provided in Article 22, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and declaring the patent in question completely invalid. Bosheng Company indicated that it would file an administrative lawsuit.

It is further found that Case No. 368, which involves the same allegedly infringing product and the 180.2 patent, is still pending first-instance trial before the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province. On January 2, 2020, Xinghao Company filed an invalidation declaration request for the 180.2 patent involved in that case, and the China National Intellectual Property Administration has not yet rendered a review decision.

It is also found that, as of the time Lianyue Company filed this application for a preservation order on November 5, 2020, a total of RMB 15.6 million had been frozen in the Alipay account balance of Lianyue Company. Of this amount, RMB 6.32 million was frozen pursuant to the property preservation measures of the court of first instance; RMB 1 million was the guarantee that Lianyue Company agreed to deposit under the "Letter of Commitment for Intellectual Property Guarantee"; and RMB 8.28 million was the amount agreed to by Lianyue Company for Alipay Company and Tmall Company to freeze, representing all sales revenue from its online shop from 10:00 p.m. on November 10, 2019.

Upon review, this Court finds that, regarding Lianyue Company's application for a preservation order, the following issues need to be examined: (I) Whether Lianyue Company, as the alleged infringer, has the standing to file an application for a preservation order; (II) Whether a preservation order restoring links should be granted in this case; (III) The determination of the amount of security in this case.

(I) Whether Lianyue Company, as the alleged infringer, has the standing to file an application for a preservation order

Article 100 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) provides: "Where a case may be difficult to enforce or may cause other damage to a party due to the acts of one party or for other reasons, the people's court may, upon the application of the other party, rule to preserve the property of the party, order the party to perform a certain act, or prohibit the party from performing a certain act; where the parties have not filed an application, the people's court may, if necessary, also rule to take preservation measures. When the people's court takes preservation measures, it may order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, the application shall be dismissed. After accepting an application, the people's court shall render a ruling within forty-eight hours in an emergency; if a preservation measure is ruled, enforcement shall commence immediately." According to the above provisions, the elements for the people's court to take a preservation order mainly include: first, the acts of one party or other reasons make the judgment difficult to enforce or cause other damage to the party; second, one party clearly applies for a preservation order, or the people's court deems it truly necessary. Obviously, the applicant for a preservation order is not limited to the plaintiff. In particular, in disputes over intellectual property infringement involving e-commerce platforms, allowing an allegedly infringing platform operator to apply for a preservation order under the conditions provided in Article 100 of the Civil Procedure Law to request the e-commerce platform operator to take preservation measures such as restoring links is of significant importance for reasonably balancing the legitimate interests of intellectual property right holders, e-commerce platform operators, and platform operators, and for promoting the healthy development of the e-commerce market.

Article 36, Paragraph 2 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Tort Liability Law) provides: "Where a network user uses network services to commit a tortious act, the aggrieved person has the right to notify the network service provider to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, and disconnection of links. If the network service provider fails to take necessary measures in a timely manner after receiving the notification, it shall be jointly and severally liable with the network user for the aggravation of the damage." Article 42 of the E-Commerce Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the E-Commerce Law) provides: "Where an intellectual property right holder believes that its intellectual property rights have been infringed, it has the right to notify the e-commerce platform operator to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnection of links, termination of transactions and services. The notification shall include preliminary evidence of the infringement. After receiving the notification, the e-commerce platform operator shall promptly take necessary measures and forward the notification to the platform operator; if it fails to take necessary measures in a timely manner, it shall be jointly and severally liable with the platform operator for the aggravation of the damage." According to the above provisions, when an e-commerce platform operator receives a notification from an intellectual property right holder containing preliminary evidence of infringement, it has a statutory obligation to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnection of links, termination of transactions and services. However, neither the Tort Liability Law nor the E-Commerce Law provides for the circumstances under which an e-commerce platform operator may take measures such as restoring links upon the application of a platform operator during litigation. Since intellectual property rights acquired through administrative authorization, such as patents, may become unstable during civil infringement litigation due to invalidation declarations, administrative litigation, and other procedures, and the operating conditions of the platform operator may also undergo significant changes during litigation, where a platform operator, due to an emergency, would suffer irreparable harm to its legitimate interests if the link is not restored, and applies to the people's court for a preservation order requiring the e-commerce platform operator to take measures such as restoring links, the people's court shall accept the application and examine it in accordance with Article 100 of the Civil Procedure Law and the relevant judicial interpretations.

In this case, the patent in question is a utility model patent. Although the court of first instance found infringement and Tmall Company deleted the sales link for the allegedly infringing product, the patent in question was declared completely invalid during the second-instance trial, and its validity is in an uncertain state due to Bosheng Company's impending administrative lawsuit. Under these circumstances, Lianyue Company, as the party whose product link was deleted, has the standing to file an application for a preservation order to restore the link.

(II) Whether a preservation order restoring links should be granted in this case

Article 7 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Reviewing Cases of Preservation Orders in Intellectual Property Disputes (hereinafter referred to as the Preservation Provisions) provides: "When reviewing an application for a preservation order, the people's court shall comprehensively consider the following factors: (1) whether the applicant's request has a factual basis and legal foundation, including whether the validity of the intellectual property right sought to be protected is stable; (2) whether the failure to take a preservation order would cause irreparable harm to the applicant's legitimate rights and interests or make it difficult to enforce the judgment; (3) whether the harm to the applicant caused by the failure to take a preservation order would exceed the harm to the respondent caused by taking the preservation order; (4) whether taking the preservation order would harm the public interest; and (5) other factors that should be considered." According to the above provisions, in determining whether to grant a preservation order for restoring links upon the application of an allegedly infringing party in an intellectual property infringement dispute involving an e-commerce platform, the following factors should be mainly considered: 1. whether the applicant's request has a factual basis and legal foundation; 2. whether the failure to restore the link would cause irreparable harm to the applicant; 3. whether the harm that restoring the link may cause to the patentee would exceed the harm that not restoring the link would cause to the alleged infringer; 4. whether restoring the link would harm the public interest; 5. whether there are other circumstances that render restoration inappropriate. Specifically to this case, the analysis is as follows:

1. Whether Lianyue Company's request has a factual basis and legal foundation. This case is a dispute over infringement of a utility model patent. The granting of utility model patents in China does not undergo substantive examination, and their rights are relatively unstable. In order to balance the interests of the patentee and those of competitors and the public, and to maintain a normal and orderly online operating environment, when a patentee requests an e-commerce platform operator to delete a sales link for a product suspected of infringing a utility model patent, it should submit a patent evaluation report issued by the patent administrative department. If the patentee fails to submit such a report without justifiable reasons, the e-commerce platform operator may refuse to delete the link, unless the court finds infringement after trial. In this case, Tmall Company deleted the sales link for the allegedly infringing product in a timely manner after the court of first instance found infringement. However, during the second-instance trial, the patent in question was declared completely invalid by the China National Intellectual Property Administration for lack of novelty, and Bosheng Company is about to file an administrative lawsuit, leaving the validity of the patent uncertain. As of November 5, 2020, due to the present case and Case No. 368, a total of RMB 15.6 million had been frozen in Lianyue Company's Alipay account balance, severely affecting its normal business operations. Under these circumstances, Lianyue Company's request for Tmall Company to restore the product link has a factual basis and legal foundation.

2. Whether the failure to restore the link would cause irreparable harm to the applicant. In disputes over intellectual property infringement involving e-commerce platforms, deleting, blocking, or disconnecting product sales links not only prevents the product from being sold on the e-commerce platform but also affects the product's previously accumulated traffic, search weight, and account rating, thereby reducing the platform operator's competitive advantage in the market. Therefore, in determining "irreparable harm," consideration should be given to whether any of the following circumstances exist: (1) whether the failure to take a preservation order would cause irreparable harm to the applicant's rights of a personal nature, such as goodwill; (2) whether the failure to take a preservation order would cause the applicant to suffer a serious loss of market competitive advantage or business opportunities, making it impossible to accurately calculate the amount of loss even if monetary compensation could be sought due to an erroneous deletion of a link.

In this case, the allegedly infringing product was primarily sold through Lianyue Company's involved online shop on "Tmall.com." According to the facts found at first instance, as of November 13, 2019, the cumulative sales volume of the allegedly infringing product was 283,693 units; as of December 4, 2019, when the court of first instance organized the parties to exchange evidence, the cumulative sales volume was 352,996 units; as of January 13, 2020, the date of the first-instance trial, the cumulative sales volume was 594,347 units. This demonstrates, on the one hand, the large sales volume of the allegedly infringing product, and on the other hand, its significant accumulated traffic and search weight, indicating that disconnecting the sales link has a substantial impact on its online sales interests. In particular, during specific sales opportunities such as "Double 11," whether the link is restored will have a significant impact on the alleged infringer's commercial interests. Under circumstances where the validity of the patent in question is uncertain, restoring the link through a preservation order allows the platform operator to resume normal operations during specific sales opportunities such as "Double 11," thereby preventing irreparable harm to its interests.

3. Whether the harm that restoring the link may cause to the patentee would exceed the harm that not restoring the link would cause to the alleged infringer.

In this case, although the allegedly infringing product and the patented product are of the same type, there are numerous similar products on the market, and restoring the link will not lead to the complete substitution of Bosheng Company's patented product. Furthermore, this Court has already taken into account the potential losses that restoring the link may cause to Bosheng Company and will freeze the corresponding amount in Lianyue Company's Alipay account as well as the profits obtainable from continued sales after restoration, to which Lianyue Company has explicitly agreed. Under these circumstances, compared with the impact of not restoring the link on Lianyue Company's normal operations, the harm that restoring the link may cause to Bosheng Company is relatively minor.

4. Whether restoring the link would harm the public interest.

In patent infringement disputes, the public interest generally considers public health, environmental protection, and other significant societal interests. The allegedly infringing product in this case is a mop bucket used for daily household activities. When considering whether to restore the link, an important factor is whether doing so would affect public health or the environment, particularly whether it would cause undue harm to consumers' persons or property. In this case, there is no evidence indicating that the allegedly infringing product would cause such harm to the public interest.

5. Whether there are other circumstances that render restoration inappropriate.

In this case, the main ground on which Bosheng Company argued against restoring the link was that, in addition to allegedly infringing the patent right in suit, the accused infringing product also allegedly infringed Bosheng Company's Patent No. 180.2 in Case No. 368, and Patent No. 180.2 is currently still valid. In this regard, this Court is of the opinion that, first, Case No. 368 is still pending at first instance, and whether the accused infringing product constitutes infringement and whether the prior art defense is established remain uncertain. Second, in Case No. 368, Bosheng Company's claim for damages has already been secured by the preservation measure of freezing RMB 3.16 million in the Alipay account balance of Lianyue Company. Third, when determining the amount of security for the preservation of conduct in this case, this Court has taken into account the circumstances of Case No. 368 and appropriately increased the security amount provided by Lianyue Company, and has frozen the obtainable profits of Lianyue Company from continued sales after restoration of the link. Although the preservation of conduct measure in this case is for the purpose of the instant litigation and the security amount is frozen until the effective date of the judgment in this case, should Case No. 368 still be pending at that time, Bosheng Company may protect its legitimate rights and interests in that case by applying for measures such as preservation of conduct, and the court will decide whether to take preservation of conduct measures based on the circumstances of that case. Therefore, there is no situation in which the rights enjoyed by Bosheng Company under Patent No. 180.2 would be difficult to protect. In conclusion, the fact that the accused infringing product is also involved in another lawsuit for allegedly infringing Patent No. 180.2 does not affect the adoption of the preservation of conduct measure in this case. No other circumstances exist in this case that are not appropriate for restoring the link.

(3) Determination of the Security Amount in this Case

The determination of the security amount for preservation of conduct must be both reasonable and effective. It is necessary to consider the damages that may be caused to the respondent after the implementation of the preservation of conduct measure, and also to prevent an excessively high security amount from unreasonably affecting the applicant's production and operation. In patent infringement disputes involving e-commerce platforms, the determination of the security amount for the preservation measure of restoring the product link should, on the one hand, consider the losses that may be caused to the right holder after restoration of the link, ensuring that the right holder's right to separately claim compensation for such losses is fully protected; on the other hand, it should also reasonably determine the obtainable profits of the applicant after restoration of the link, avoiding an unreasonable impact on the applicant's capital recovery and subsequent operations due to freezing an excessive amount of sales revenue. Specifically in this case, Bosheng Company claimed economic damages of RMB 3.16 million from the alleged infringer in both this case and Case No. 368, and the court of first instance has already taken property preservation measures. However, taking into account factors such as the relatively large sales volume of the accused infringing product before the link was removed and the likelihood that restoration of the link may expand Bosheng Company's losses, in order to protect the patentee's interests to the greatest extent, this Court will determine the security amount by comprehensively considering factors including Bosheng Company's compensation claims in the two cases and the obtainable profits of Lianyue Company after restoration of the link. Given that Lianyue Company's obtainable profits will increase continuously with product sales, in addition to a fixed security bond, this Court will add a dynamic security bond. Since Lianyue Company's sales revenue also includes costs, management expenses, etc., to prevent an excessively high security amount from unreasonably affecting Lianyue Company's production and operation, this Court, after considering the patent contribution rates of the patents involved in this case and Case No. 368, appropriately determines the dynamic security bond as 50% of Lianyue Company's sales revenue.

In conclusion, Lianyue Company's application requesting Tmall Company to restore the sales link of the accused infringing product complies with legal provisions and should be granted. Pursuant to Article 100 and Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 7 and Article 11 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Examination of Preservation of Conduct Cases in Intellectual Property Disputes, it is hereby ordered as follows:

1. The respondent, Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd., shall immediately restore the sales link of the accused infringing product of the applicant, Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., on the "Tmall.com" shopping platform;

2. The balance of RMB 6.32 million in the Alipay account under the name of the applicant, Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., shall be frozen until the date on which the judgment in this case becomes effective;

3. From the date of restoration of the sales link of the accused infringing product to the date on which the judgment in this case becomes effective, if 50% of the total sales revenue of the accused infringing product of the applicant, Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., after restoration of the link exceeds RMB 6.32 million, then 50% of the sales revenue exceeding that amount shall remain in its Alipay account and shall not be withdrawn.

This order shall be executed immediately.

The application fee for this case is RMB 30, to be borne by the applicant, Yongkang Lianyue Industry & Trade Co., Ltd.

If any party refuses to accept this order, it may apply to this Court for a review within five days from the date of receipt of the order. Execution of the order shall not be suspended during the review period.
